items.title: I hate it when they do this!
items.summary:
PSA to all the AI companies:

Please stop announcing features like they’re live when they’re still rolling out “over the coming weeks.” 

This happened for like 4 different demos in my recent AI news roundup video...

Is it so hard to just make an announcement when I can actually use the new feature 😅

#ai #ainews #claude
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: If I'm being honest, like a little personal pet peeve of buying it, I don't think I'm alone in this. I wish companies would announce it when it's ready as opposed to say, "Here's something we're doing but not yet. It's coming in the future." Anthropic announced that Claude Co-work and their chat are now just one thing, so you don't need to switch between them. But when I open the Claude app, I still see a chat and Co-work option here. When I scroll down on the article, this is rolling out to Pro and Max plans first. I am on a $200 a month Max plan and I still don't have it yet. The title of this blog post is Claude Co-work and chat are now one Claude. No, they're not now one Claude. They're going to be in the future after it finishes its roll out to Pro and Max plans. items.title: This Robot Looks DEMONIC... On Purpose?
items.summary:
This robot looks straight up like a fantasy movie villain, but it was designed like that on purpose.

Despite how it looks, the Threehalves robot's design actually makes perfect sense: four legs for stability, tools that attach directly to its wrists, and horns that house cameras for a remote operator.

The goal is to let skilled workers tackle dangerous jobs from a safe distance, like wildfire zones, collapsed buildings, and toxic environments.

It’s still a half-built proof of concept. But this is the kind of robotics idea I want to see work. Even if I’d absolutely run the other way if I saw it in the woods.

#Robotics #FutureTech #AInews #ai
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: This is the weirdest thing I saw this week. A California-based company built a robot that looks super creepy on purpose. It's called three halves and its design choices are actually pretty genius. The idea is to send it into places humans shouldn't have to go, like wildfire zones, collapsed buildings, toxic environments, and other extremely dangerous job sites. Its four legs give it a wide, stable base for moving across rough terrain, and if it loses power, its joints lock. So, unlike a two-legged robot, it shouldn't immediately just collapse. The human-like torso lets it work in environments designed for us, but instead of fragile robotic hands, its wrists connect directly to tools like chainsaws and drills and impact wrenches. And those massive horns actually contain cameras that let the remote operator see around the robot and monitor where it's stepping. A skilled worker controls it from a safe distance with a joystick. Now, this is still only a half-built proof of concept, but if this thing ever becomes fully operational, seeing a 7-ft tall robot sent to our carrying a chainsaw through the woods might actually be helpful, despite how terrifying it may look.
